newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's ANC clashes with Reserve Bank on jobs.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's ANC clashes with Reserve Bank on jobs.

text.p: South Africa's African National Congress (ANC) party and its labour and communist allies fired a broadside at the Reserve Bank on Friday for speaking out of turn on proposed labour legislation.

The ANC-led alliance, which also includes the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) and the South African Communist Party, attacked the central bank for an "inappropriate intervention" on labour policy in its latest Quarterly Bulletin.

The bulletin, published late on Thursday, highlighted the inability of the economy to generate enough jobs to absorb South Africa's unemployed and went on to question the impact of the the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill, published in April.

The Bank said that implementation of proposals including a shorter working week, increased leave arrangements, a higher premium for overtime and a training levy could have an adverse impact on formal-sector employment.
"The Reserve Bank, which is supposed, constitutionally, to be independent, has no business whatsover intervening in a biased way into this matter," the alliance secretariat said in a statement.

Feelings over the proposed labour legislation are running high in South Africa. Cosatu held a one-day national stoppage to press its claims for a better deal for workers earlier this month and is currently threatening further action.
